overview: The Medford City Council met to consider special permits, ordinance referrals, and several state legislative resolutions, alongside major debates on public participation and housing policy. Key outcomes included referring a rental registry proposal to committee, amending council rules on public comment limits, discussing school budget deficits with local teachers, and approving climate and education resolutions.

items.title: Dedications, Ramadan Recognition, and Minutes Approval
items.summary: The council approved resolutions honoring former Mayor Jack McGlynn and commemorating Ramadan, and approved the meeting records from March 19, 2024.

items.title: Reports of Committees
items.summary: The council approved committee reports covering budget recommendations, food truck regulations, linkage fees, election updates, short-term rentals, and fee schedules.

items.title: Special Permit for Raising Cane's Signage
items.summary: Approved a special permit for additional on-premises signage for Raising Cane's at 760 Fellsway following a continued public hearing.

items.title: Linkage Fee Ordinance Amendments
items.summary: Referred proposed technical amendments and an affordable housing allocation for the linkage fee ordinance to the Community Development Board.

items.title: Rental Registry Ordinance Proposal
items.summary: Referred a proposed rental registry ordinance to the Planning and Permitting Committee following extensive public comment and council debate.

items.title: Amendments to City Council Rules on Public Participation
items.summary: Approved amendments to City Council Rule 16 regarding public participation time limits, alongside a B-paper creating a new committee referral agenda heading.

items.title: State "Make Polluters Pay" Legislation Support
items.summary: Approved a resolution supporting state legislation to establish a climate change superfund financed by major fossil fuel companies.

items.title: School Budget Shortfall Discussion
items.summary: Discussed school budget deficit projections, ESSER funding expiration, and staffing concerns with Medford Teachers Association representatives, placing the communication on file.

items.title: Opposition to Quabbin Reservoir Landfill
items.summary: Approved a resolution opposing a proposed landfill in Hardwick near the Quabbin Reservoir watershed.

items.title: Support for CHERISH Act
items.summary: Approved a resolution supporting state passage of the CHERISH Act to increase funding for public higher education.

items.title: Human Rights Ordinance and Council Listening Sessions
items.summary: Referred resolutions to modernize the Human Rights Commission ordinance and establish city council listening sessions to the Resident Services and Public Engagement Committee.
